source_statement: In triangle ABC, a circle ω with center O passes through B and C and intersects segments AB and AC again at B ′ and C ′ , respectively. Suppose that the circles with diameters BB ′ and CC ′ are externally tangent to each other at T . If AB = 18, AC = 36, and AT = 12, compute AO.

clause_ledger.source: triangle ABC and circle omega centered at O through B,C
clause_ledger.dsl: fix AB=18, parameterize C on the AC=36 ray, and construct omega as Circumcircle(B,B',C); O and r are derived, while the original circle constraints remain

clause_ledger.source: omega intersects segments AB and AC again at B',C'
clause_ledger.dsl: B'=Point(bp,0), C'=q*C are the stated segment points and remain constrained on omega

clause_ledger.source: diameter circles BB' and CC' externally tangent at T
clause_ledger.dsl: construct the two diameter-circle centers/radii and construct their external tangency point T on the center segment; the original tangency constraints remain
direct distance constraints and Distance(A,O) answer
